title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) that measured validator utility in a generate–verify–repair (GVR) NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a synthetic intent→configuration task bank and the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter with declared model gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 deterministic pairs (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) marked every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, Guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (target = 10 percentage points) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We present preregistered design details, complete execution accounting, an artifact-grounded validator-trace exemplar, exact quantitative results, diagnostic interpretation of the ceiling outcome, reproducible follow-up prescriptions (fault-injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison), and explicit threats to validity. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied evidence bundle and are referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and problem statement. Operational NetOps automation requires reliable acceptance criteria before committing LLM-generated configurations. Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) pipelines are a prominent operational pattern: an LLM proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator enforces mechanistic constraints (syntax, required-command coverage, policy invariants), and a repair or human-gate is invoked if the validator rejects the candidate. Prior system and benchmark work motivate verifier insertion but do not provide standardized, preregistered measurements of validator coverage, false-positive/false-negative rates (FP/FN), detection latency, or predictive utility for end-to-end guarded success in realistic NetOps tasks [1]–[5].

Research question and contribution. We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to answer: Can a multidimensional validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact proxy) predict end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single raw verifier pass rate? The confirmatory estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded). Our contribution is an exact, artifact-grounded report of the preregistered paired experiment, the degenerate ceiling outcome observed across all 200 pairs, diagnostic analysis of why the ceiling arose, and artifact-grounded preregistered prescriptions required to estimate validator FP/FN and repair value in future runs.
sections.related_work:
Positioning. Work on GVR and verifier-augmented pipelines in code and systems domains documents how deterministic checks and repair guidance reduce stochastic generator errors and enable deterministic acceptance criteria [R. Cadenas, SSRN 2026]. NetOps- and AIOps-oriented benchmarks and prototype systems (OpsEval, FaulT-Bench, ITBench-type suites) highlight ticket noise, false-premise reports, and wrong-but-plausible agent outputs that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier layers [K.-H. Tseng et al., arXiv:2608.27021; Y. Liu et al., arXiv:2310.07637]. Recent agentic-orchestrator and self-healing proposals advocate deterministic validators, auditable decision traces, and repair scaffolds to reduce silent failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [R. S. Babu & A. Agrawal, arXiv:2606.01416]. Surveys of LLMs for telecommunications recommend careful metricization of verification cost versus nominal correctness [H. Zhou et al., IEEE Commun. Surveys & Tutorials, 2024].

Gap and careful claim framing. These prior records establish that verifier layers are architecturally valuable and that controlled benchmarks reveal substantive failure modes, but they do not supply a standardized empirically estimable validator-metric suite for NetOps GVR flows with preregistered paired inference. We therefore designed AC-2026-03 to begin measuring validator utility under strict preregistration and reproducible archive practices. We intentionally avoid extrapolating beyond what the cited literature supports: prior demonstrations are treated as motivation and architectural precedent, not proof of validator coverage in heterogeneous production NetOps.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design details. The experiment was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key frozen design choices (excerpted from the preregistration manifest): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false (explicit). The primary confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired binary success (validator.valid), with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power plan targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power under conservative assumptions (baseline p = 0.50) using n = 200.

Task bank, generator, and constraints. Tasks were sampled deterministically from a synthetic bank produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an intent, allowed_fields/allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. These structured intents are mechanistically checkable by the deterministic validator and were selected via a preregistered deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1). Contamination/exclusion rules (duplicate SHA-256, semantic-similarity cosine > 0.95) were preregistered; no exclusions occurred in this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). We explicitly report that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider-side sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider sampling nondeterminism remains possible and the execution manifest records provider-call audit events to support traceability. The adapter's provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared initial generation per task.

Validator and scoring rule. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when present. The preregistered binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call for rejected candidates; repairs would be recorded in repair_provider_trace fields and repair_applied toggled accordingly.

Execution controls and missingness. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The missingness plan specified primary complete-pair analysis and a sensitivity analysis treating incomplete pairs as failures. The execution manifest shows completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. All raw outputs, per-episode validator traces, provider-call traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and referenced in the evidence manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination exclusions or near-duplicate exclusions occurred.

Primary confirmatory result (artifact-grounded). The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. The precise numeric artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match the reported values.

Representative validator-trace exemplar (artifact verbatim). To illustrate validator semantics and why no repairs were triggered, we include a compact verbatim excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (representative pair). Key archived fields (verbatim):
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - observed_touched_field_count: 3
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
  - validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  - validator_version: 5.0

Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode. Representative per-episode JSON blobs and shared-initial response text for this and other exemplar pairs are available in the execution bundle (execution/responses/*, execution/scoring/*) and are referenced by artifact hashes in the manifest.

Exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives). Detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative because repair_applied = false for all episodes. The raw execution bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl) and analysis artifacts contain full per-episode traces to support reanalysis under alternative scoring rules or injected-fault scenarios.
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling occurred (artifact-grounded diagnosis). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical generated candidate for each task; thus any paired difference could only arise from deterministic validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling). The degenerate all-valid outcome stems from three artifact-evidenced factors recorded in the archive: (1) the deterministic task generator produced intent→configuration references for the selected seeds that the model reproduced in sampled candidates which satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) eliminated generator variability as a source of disagreements; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic checks and therefore cannot detect some classes of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent) absent an external intent model or operator signal. Together these explain why no repairs occurred and the confirmatory test could not detect the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement.

Implications for experimental design. The paired shared_initial_candidate design is methodologically strong for isolating downstream repair effects, but it concentrates ceiling risk when generator and validator align. To produce estimable FP/FN and repair-utility statistics, future preregistered arms must alter baseline invalidity prevalence or sampling variability (artifact-supported prescriptions below). Our artifact bundle supports deterministic task replacement and contamination checks necessary to implement these arms reproducibly.

Artifact-grounded follow-up prescriptions (preregistered):
  1) Fault-injection arm (deterministic): deterministically inject controlled faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This will create measurable baseline invalidity and allow guarded repair benefit to be observed and quantified in paired comparisons.
  2) Multi-sample generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (independent sampling seeds recorded). Permit the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved candidate among k draws or to invoke repair; this will expose generator variability and create opportunities for validator rejection and repair.
  3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family. Cross-validator comparisons will estimate sensitivity of FP/FN to validator design choices and improve external validity beyond a single validator-model pairing.
Each prescription is directly implementable with the archived adapter semantics and task-generation utilities recorded in the bundle.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed mechanistic checks and no repairs were applied; guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This artifact-grounded result demonstrates that preregistered paired designs isolate repair effects but are vulnerable to ceiling outcomes when generator and validator align and when only one sample per task is taken. We publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and to enable the community to run the concrete, preregistered follow-up arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) necessary to obtain estimable validator FP/FN, detection-latency, and repair-utility statistics. The archived bundle contains the exact per-episode traces, provider-call audits, and analysis logs referenced above and in the Disclosure Statement; those artifacts should be used to reproduce and extend the measurement program described here.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): Declared model and provider: gpt-5-mini via provider bundle 'openai_responses'. Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). Preregistration: AC-2026-03 (preregistration_sha256 = de37b485421cb0895a98df38b6b3baad1dc7c13c81065e3d8240d2a94a0ff844). Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, execution, analysis, internal peer review and manuscript drafting without manual editing of technical content. Sampling/generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation per task reused for baseline and guarded); execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Call budget and usage (preregistered): maximum_model_calls = 400; actual model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). All raw outputs, per-episode validator traces, execution manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json). No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
